first_impression.reaction: Mykonos. I'd have thought of nightclubs, honestly. But the opening is sensible: three decisions, in order, legal or symbolic first. Nobody's gushing at me. The key takeaways even say to ask about deposits and cancellation and get it in writing. I'll read the lot.

journey.quote: Ask every venue about deposits, cancellation, exclusive use and music times, and get the answers in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: Deposits and cancellation, right up the top. That's the first thing my husband will ask, and it's already there.

journey.section: Five venues to start your shortlist
journey.quote: Ceremonies take place on The Ocean Balcony, just above Psarou beach, for up to 60 guests, and the wedding party can then move to the L'Archipel restaurant and pool area for up to 120.
journey.reaction: Real numbers. Sixty for the ceremony is tight with both families, so that's a conversation to have early. Useful.

journey.quote: Plan water, hats, light fabrics, shade and air-conditioned rest for guests, and set a summer ceremony later in the day.
journey.reaction: Mum can't do midday heat. Air-conditioned rest and a later ceremony, exactly what I'd want someone to plan for.

journey.quote: Keep travel insurance in place for everyone travelling, and check the advice again before you fly.
journey.reaction: Heat, wildfires, earthquakes, currents, one after the other. A lot to take in, but it's calm, from the government's own advice, and it ends with insurance for everyone. I'd rather know.

journey.quote: Guests flying from Australia arrive tired, and some will be older or less steady on stairs.
journey.reaction: That's my mother and my aunt. Said plainly, without making me feel fussy for raising it.

journey.quote: It also has accessible travel information for passengers with reduced mobility, worth sending to any guest who needs help on arrival
journey.reaction: Good. I'll send that to my sister, who's travelling with Mum.

journey.quote: For guests with mobility needs or a tight connection, the flight is the steadier choice.
journey.reaction: Carrying your own bags up ferry stairs with a walking frame? No. Mum flies. Settled.

journey.section: Transfers and access to ask about
journey.quote: How far is the nearest point a car can reach, and how do guests with limited mobility get from there to the ceremony?
journey.reaction: That's my question, almost word for word. I'll ask it of every venue.

journey.quote: Requests go on the Document Legalisation Request Form, signed in front of an authorised witness, and can be lodged by appointment at an Australian Passport Office, at many Australian embassies and consulates overseas, or by registered mail to the Authentications Section in Melbourne or Sydney; a fee applies.
journey.reaction: I read this part twice. CNI, apostille, notary, authentication. If my daughter signs at the registry in Melbourne first, I suspect most of this doesn't apply to us, but nobody tells me I can skip it.

journey.quote: A foreign marriage certificate is usually accepted as proof of the marriage, but it may not work as proof of a name change.
journey.reaction: Wouldn't have thought of that. She'll want her passport changed. Good catch.

journey.section: House rules to agree before you book
journey.quote: Cancellation. Which payments are refundable, and what happens if you need to move or cancel the date?
journey.reaction: Yes. If someone falls ill and we have to move the date, what do we lose? That's the question, and it's on the list.

journey.section: House rules to agree before you book
journey.quote: Get the answers in the contract or a written confirmation, not a chat thread.
journey.reaction: My husband will underline that twice.

journey.section: Choosing where to marry on Mykonos
journey.quote: Once you have an area and a style in mind, talk to Wonderland Concierge.
journey.reaction: Wonderland Concierge here, Wedded Concierge at the bottom. Are they the same thing? Small, but when I'm handing over money I like the name to stay the same.

journey.quote: The fee is agreed in writing before any work begins, and every inclusion is confirmed in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: One person, Australian dollars, fee in writing first. That's most of what I need. I'd still want a phone call before a cent goes anywhere.

unanswered_questions: If my daughter marries legally in Melbourne first, which parts of the documents section can we ignore?
Are the venue contracts in English, and are they in euros or AUD?
Who do I ring if something goes wrong at 2am Greek time?
Is the first step with the Wedded Advisor a phone call, before anything is booked or paid?

turn_offs_found.quote: Requests go on the Document Legalisation Request Form, signed in front of an authorised witness, and can be lodged by appointment at an Australian Passport Office, at many Australian embassies and consulates overseas, or by registered mail to the Authentications Section in Melbourne or Sydney; a fee applies.
turn_offs_found.why: Long, unbroken paragraphs are one of my turn-offs, and on the iPad this one is a wall: one sentence with three ways to lodge a form. I lost my place. Split into short points, I'd follow it and forward it to my husband.

would_share_with: My husband, with the house-rules questions, especially deposits and cancellation
My sister, who's looking after Mum, with the heat advice, ferry stairs, airport accessibility link and access questions
My daughter, with the symbolic-ceremony paragraph and the name-change point

cta_reaction.quote: Your Wedded Advisor is one person, start to finish, who works in your time zone and quotes in AUD.
cta_reaction.why: One person, my time zone, AUD, fee in writing. That's what I want from whoever we pay. I'd click if I knew a real person would ring me first and could tell me which of these terraces Mum can actually get to.

top_3_changes: At the top of 'Steps for Australian couples', add one sentence saying couples who marry legally in Australia and hold a symbolic ceremony on the island can skip most of this section.
Break the Document Legalisation paragraph into short bullet points (form, witness, where to lodge, fee) so it reads on an iPad.
Use one name for the concierge service throughout: the primary CTA says 'Wonderland Concierge' but the closing says 'Wedded Concierge'.

checks.check: Every journey point, turn-off and CTA reaction has an exact quote from the draft
Stayed in character as Margaret (funding parent, practical, reads top to bottom on an iPad, mother uses a walking frame)
No invented brand facts; missing business details listed as unanswered questions only
HTML comments, image slots and VERIFY markers treated as invisible
Title, deferred business details, sourcing, not-published lines and absent prices not raised as must-fix, per orchestrator
Journey types limited to the allowed enum; every turn-off has a why

open_questions.question: The primary CTA link text says 'Wonderland Concierge' while brand terms and the closing use 'Wedded Concierge'. Check against brand terms. Contract language, on-the-day contact and a phone-first step are business details and deferred.

assumptions: Margaret reads the whole article on an iPad because her daughter sent it, and her own mother uses a walking frame (per voice samples).
Prices are deliberately not printed, so their absence was not raised.
